segments.speaker: char-visitor

segments.text: 人閉卷。人持卷，開門。人出門，閉門。安視卷，寧視人。人視燈，問。
安指書，客持書。安無書，客有書。人視客。客持紙，紙在手，紙有姓。
寧還燈，人取燈。人持燈，視寧。安指燈，人問。
人還燈，寧取燈。寧假燈，人持卷。客視紙，安視書。人指書，客開書。寧持燈，燈不明。

segments.text: 客持書，安取書。安假書，寧持燈。安持書，書在手，安視破葉。客持紙，視姓。人持卷，安持書。卷有字，書有字。紙有少字，書有多字。
人指破葉，安視半字。人識半字，寧視書。客開帙，人視帙字。
寧：「破葉有半字，半葉有半字。寧識半字。」
segments.speaker: char-ning

segments.text: 寧指半字，安視寧。破葉有半字，紙有姓。帙字少。客閉帙，持紙。安視半字，識半字。人視書，問。
安閉書，持書。寧持燈，火不明。人視火，開門。人入門，持卷。門內有火，火明。人呼安，安應。安持書入門。人呼寧，寧應。寧持燈入門。客在門外，持紙。人呼客，客應。客持帙入門。客持紙。人閉門。安視火，寧視書。

sections.title: The indoor comparison distinguishes the visible evidence from a missing counterpart

segments.text: 人開卷，安開書。火明，寧指半字。寧視葉。卷有全葉，書有破葉。人視全葉，寧視半字。人視卷，視破葉。安持書，寧識半字。客持紙，視姓。人取紙，客視紙。人視姓，還紙。客取紙，持紙。人視卷，視書。
人指卷，寧視全葉。人指書，安視破葉。
寧視卷，安視書。紙有姓，破葉無姓。
寧：「父持二葉。全葉有名，半葉有名。」
segments.speaker: char-ning

segments.text: 安：「母在家，持小書。先生在家，有紙。」
segments.speaker: char-an

segments.text: 人視安，指破葉。安指書，人視卷。寧持燈，客持紙。
安還書，客取書。客閉大書，持書。寧還燈，人取燈。人持燈，安視火。寧指全葉，人視寧。人閉卷，問。
人持卷，寧取卷。寧假卷，持卷。安視卷，客視書。人指書，問。

grammar.title: 誰持燈？
grammar.rule: 誰｜持燈？寧｜持燈。書｜在｜何處？主，誰也？
grammar.note_en:
Study Chapter6 in How to read before the story. The three packets preserve eighteen retrievals and add explicit worked question/reply contrasts, borrowing, recognition, completeness and contextual reference. All ten extra earlier-meaning retrievals supplement the normal thirty workbook items and A8/B8/C6. Mandarin tone-marked pinyin is a citation reading convention, not a reconstruction of ancient pronunciation.

A subject is the person or thing whose action is stated. In 誰呼？ “Who calls?”, 誰 shuí replaces the unknown subject, without an extra verb meaning do. 安呼 “An calls” supplies the name in the same place. Compare 誰持燈？ “Who holds the lamp?” and 寧持燈 “Ning holds the lamp.” The question is not asking whether the lamp exists or who owns it. This chapter uses 誰 as subject or nominal predicate, not an untaught interrogative-preposition system.

A nominal predicate states an identity with a noun. 主，誰也？ means “The owner—who is it?” The unknown identity 誰 replaces a name and the known nominal ending 也 remains. 安不知主 means “An does not know the owner”: 不 denies 知 zhī, knowing, rather than directly denying the noun 主 zhǔ. Do not replace this with an embedded know-who question. Knowing who holds an object is not knowing its owner. The reader’s accusation 安，盜也。寧，盜也, “An is a thief; Ning is a thief,” is attributed speech, not an established fact or a new verb steal.

In 書在何處？ “Where is the book?”, 在 retains the location predicate and 何處 hé chù means what place. The book is outside before the person opens the gate. Later 葉在何處？ “Where are the leaves?” elicits 葉在家 “The leaves are at home,” the known distant family household. The leaves have not arrived at the new gate. Every 何 here belongs to this bounded where family; its broader how/why applications are not yet executed teaching. No prepositional fronting, embedded question, possessive 之 or general topic ellipsis is assumed.

問 wèn frames a question and 答 dá frames a spoken answer: 人問。安答, “The person asks; An answers.” Direct quotation is kept separate. 應 yìng still means responding to a call. A negative report of knowledge is a proper answer; nobody must guess an unread name. 指 zhǐ means point to the named object: 人指破葉 “The person points to the damaged leaf.” It does not introduce a new body-part word finger. In 寧識半字 “Ning recognises the half-character,” 識 shí concerns the particular identifying mark, not general literacy or a decoded unseen surname. Contrast 寧不知主 “Ning does not know the owner.” Ning recalls 破葉有半字，半葉有半字, “The damaged leaf has a half-character; the half-leaf has a half-character,” from the earlier on-page comparison at home. She recognises the particular mark without bringing that absent leaf into this scene or proving the works identical.

假 jiǎ is borrowing or having on loan, with the borrower as subject. In 人：「誰假燈？」寧：「寧假燈。」 “Who will borrow the lamp?”—“Ning will borrow it,” the holder’s question is a prospective offer, followed by Ning taking it. The narrated willingness and handoff establish a loan now; taking the lamp in chapter5 did not. Likewise the messenger offers the large book for inspection and An later returns it. At the end this reader offers his separate fascicle and Ning borrows it. The text does not identify this man with the family’s teacher or merge their separate fascicles. A current holder’s offer does not prove ultimate ownership.

卷全，書不全 means “The fascicle is complete; the book is incomplete.” 全 is the earlier whole/complete quality in the positive and negative predicate family. 卷有全葉 “The fascicle has whole leaves” and 書有破葉 “The book has a damaged leaf” support a physical comparison, not proof of identical works. The bounded substantive 一半 yī bàn means one half, with the already known 一 and 半. In the closing 書不全。一半在門內，一半在何處？ “The book is incomplete. One half is inside the gate; where is the other half?”, the paired one-half statements distinguish the present part from its missing counterpart. This is the reader’s explicit assessment and unanswered question, not narrator proof from a damaged leaf alone, a named owner or matching works. Practise this one complementary pair; wider quantity patterns will come later.

Movements and custody remain explicit. The reader closes and carries his fascicle out, then reopens the gate for better indoor light. Calls are pragmatically invitations in that opened-gate sequence; 呼 itself still means call. An enters holding the large book; Ning enters with the lamp; the messenger enters with wrapper and sheet. The gate then closes. The messenger regains the large book and the reader regains the lamp. The reader briefly takes the surname sheet, looks at its surname and returns it without reading an unprinted identity. Ning ends holding the newly borrowed fascicle, not the teacher’s distant fascicle.

C.title: Pensa C — Answer the questions and follow their consequences
C.instruction: Answer each story question or continue its cue in complete Chinese statements. Retrieve the following event or contrast, not a bare name, yes/no or invented owner. Models are examples, not exact strings.

model_answers: 寧還燈，人取燈。人問，寧假燈。
items.rubric: Respond with the return and new borrowing exchange, beyond merely naming the holder. No ultimate lamp-owner identity.
Distinguish recognising the damaged identifying mark from knowing the owner; include complete clauses.

model_answers: 人開門。人呼安，安應。安持書入門。
items.rubric: Retrieve the opening and a called traveller’s explicit entrance. Do not move the family or teacher.

model_answers: 葉在家。父持二葉。全葉有名，半葉有名。名同。
items.rubric: Place the old loose leaves back at the far household, then retrieve the marks or custodian. No invented matching book-owner or reputation.
Retrieve Ning’s arranged loan of this reader’s separate fascicle and the messenger’s continuing custody of the large book. These are distinct objects.

items.prompt: 書不全。一半在門內，一半在何處？安、寧、客：
model_answers: 安視人，寧視書。客持紙，視人。
items.rubric: Report the unanswered reactions after the reader explicitly contrasts one present half with the unlocated complementary half. Use complete statements, without guessing owner, surname or location. The half-book assessment belongs to the reader, not narrator-certified arithmetic.

notes: Original constructed narration. No adapted/authentic quotation, audio or generated picture. No prior introduction blocks changed; normal reading and full practice volumes remain.

The G06 clarification advances no general quantity system; no phrase-sized lexeme or self-issued exception.
All32 scheduled earlier meanings are executed in narrative and/or explicit actual preparation/practice; literal graph recurrence is only screening evidence.
Reader’s accusation is attributed. Custody, identity, recognition and ownership are kept distinct. No old-leaf/small-book/work identity or unread surname is invented.

Attempt1 requested bounded paired-half clarification adopted in G06. Reader explicitly assesses the incomplete book as one present half and asks about its complementary half; narrator does not independently certify exact loss. No general quantity system or new phrase-sized lexeme is created. Ning’s recollection follows chapter2 s008, when she saw both half-characters; she does not compare an absent leaf now.
